source: configs/cpu.yaml, the ONLY validated production profile per its own header comment ("CPU is the default because it is the only configuration actually validated in this project") -- with ONE field changed: device "cpu" -> "auto".
why_device_auto_not_cpu_or_cuda_literal: configs/gpu.yaml (device: cuda unconditional) explicitly recommends against itself on a shared machine: "On a SHARED machine prefer device: auto over cuda: it inspects free VRAM, utilization and other compute processes first, and falls back to CPU rather than competing with another project's job." This machine IS shared (Research-No.1). device=auto is genuine, already-implemented, already-validated production logic (src/doc_extraction/utils/resources.py select_device()) -- not a benchmark-special override. Verified this phase: select_device("auto") resolves to cuda right now given the actual observed GPU state (baseline_environment.json).
why_not_change_ocr_languages: docs/production-contract.md: "OCR is configured [en, vi], which is a deliberate choice for this corpus -- experiment 007 measured that swapping to a Chinese model to chase a public benchmark costs 43.6% on English and collapses English table structure from 0.715 to 0.000." OmniDocBench is majority Chinese-language content; changing ocr_languages to add zh would be exactly the prohibited benchmark-chasing change (Phase 16). ocr_languages remains ["en", "vi"], unchanged from production.
unvalidated_alternative_not_used: configs/gpu.yaml (device: cuda literal, unconditional -- would contend with another project's job if one started mid-run; auto degrades gracefully instead)
